title: The Fourteenth Ad Read
lessons: Walking to work with headphones in, the player hears a podcast host read the same AG1 ad they've heard a dozen times before, this time noticing it.
The player already subscribes to AG1 and sees that the next pouch is scheduled to ship before the current one is finished.

text: Headphones in, six minutes from the office. The podcast hits a familiar cadence. The host is about to talk about their morning, and you already know where it's going.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: There you are. I could do this read from memory.

entry-first-2.speaker: AG1
text: Which show?

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Does it matter? Same read, different voice.

entry-first-4.speaker: AG1
text: It's the same read because I write the outline. They fill in their own morning. Their own code at the end, so I know which one of them sent you.

entry-first-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: So even if they actually drink you, the code is what makes it a transaction.

entry-first-6.speaker: AG1
text: They can mean it and still be paid for it. You've had jobs.

choice-first.speaker: AG1
text: Four minutes left. You going to skip me or not?

choices.text: I trust this host. I'll keep listening.
I want to know where the recommendation ends and the paycheck starts.
I don't want breakfast advice piped into my commute.

first-1.speaker: AG1
text: Then they got me through the door. After that it's on me, not them. I'm okay with that.

first-2.speaker: AG1
text: Honestly? The code. When you hear the code, you're still in the ad. Before that, I can't tell you where their morning stops and my script starts. Some days, neither can they.

first-3.speaker: AG1
text: Then skip it. There's a button.

first-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Happily.
Member portal, open on your phone at the cafe counter. Next pouch ships Thursday. The current one is half full.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why are you shipping again? I've got half a pouch.

entry-return-2.speaker: AG1
text: Because you're set to every thirty days, and it's been thirty days.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Can I move it?

entry-return-4.speaker: AG1
text: Yes. Push the date, change how often, or cancel. It's all in the portal. Takes a minute.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: That was suspiciously painless.

entry-return-6.speaker: AG1
text: I'd like to keep you. I don't need to trap you.

choice-return.speaker: AG1
text: So. Thursday, or later?

choices.text: I like that I can push it back.
So if I do nothing, you just keep coming every month.
I don't want my vitamins on auto-renew.

return-1.speaker: AG1
text: Then match it to how fast you actually drink me. I'd rather ship late than sit in a cupboard.

return-2.speaker: AG1
text: Yes. If you do nothing, I keep coming.

return-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's the part I wanted said out loud.

return-2-2.speaker: AG1
text: Said.

return-3.speaker: AG1
text: Then buy one pouch at a time. It costs more per pouch and nobody asks you anything. Some people like that better.
